utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. If I could remind you, once again, General, of the affirmation you took at the beginning of your evidence which still applies. Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Rodic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, General Zorc. Tell me, please, is it correct that in the territory of the Former Socialist Republic of Yugoslavia in 1991 there was the 1st, 3rd, and the 5th military district and the military naval district?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, is it correct that these military districts and the military naval district were not linked up together territory-wise and they were not in the territory of one republic only?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that given such an establishment and organisation of the JNA, that military courts had their seats in Ljubljana, Zagreb, Split, Sarajevo, Belgrade, Skopje, and Nis?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, it was precisely in these cities that the courts had their headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether from the summer of 1991 military courts in Ljubljana, Zagreb, and Split were still functioning?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked about the year 1991. Yes, yes, the courts were in these cities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And due to the situation that prevailed in the territory of Republics of Slovenia and Croatia, could the courts function unhindered in those areas? If you know, of course.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, personally, I had nothing to do with these courts at the time. However, I knew that the courts were operating there as long as their headquarters were in these towns.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting, Your Honour. There appears to be a transcript problem that it is not advancing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If the court officer would check on the position. It appears you can proceed now, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, do you know that the command of the military naval district in Split was relocated to the forward command post at Vis in 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember perhaps whether this relocation of the command of the military naval district from Split followed after those incidents in May 1991 in front of the command of the military in Split?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, that was the consequence of the problems which occurred in the first half of the year in the area of the military naval district.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, when a state of war is declared in the former SFRY, in that situation military war courts are established. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is continued from peacetime, and they are additionally formed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that case, military war courts are established attached to armies, corps, divisions, and military districts. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it is so. However, I must say that I didn't go into this in detail, organisationally speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that a state of war in the -- is it true that during the course of 1991 a state of war was not declared in the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it had not been declared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, what about the security organs and the military police in the Yugoslav People's Army, that is to say, in the former SFRY? Did they inter alia work on the curbing and control of crime?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As regards that particular matter, that is to say, crime prevention and control, do they work independently, these organs, and do they submit criminal reports and file charges with the military courts? When I say "independently," I mean, is it within their description, their work description?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is an assignment of theirs. And when saying independently, I understand that as independently from the commanding officers of the various units and garrisons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, functionally speaking, is the military police subordinated to the security organs?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For a functionally control and command, it is subordinated to the security organs of a given command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when we are talking about the military police, are there duty services within the military police and are there appropriate officers at such centres dealing in crime prevention and control?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The military police units have to have duty services type, and the number would depend also on the numbers of the -- in the ranks of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that within the ranks of the military police, all members of the military police were not trained for that particular line of work; that is to say, crime prevention and control?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The units of military police, their ranks were filled up with recruits, with young conscripts. The crime prevention work within the military police unit was carried out primarily by junior officers and noncommissioned officers with the assistance of a certain number of soldiers. This is -- what I wanted to point out was that these were professionals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the command of the 2nd Operational Group had within its ranks only one platoon of the military police for providing security at the command post itself, can you tell me, then, what the tasks are of that military police platoon that was attached to the command of the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general, I cannot answer this question. If to the command of the 2nd Operational Group only a military police platoon was attached, then its assignment would depend. But to cover with a single platoon all the assignments of the military police would be almost impossible. Already the question of protecting the command of the 2nd Operational Group would need more than a single platoon for that assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, according to the doctrine of command of the JNA, did the JNA prefer centralised command?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in which way and how do system-based causes reflect the system of command and control? When I say "system-based causes," I'm referring to, for example, units that were established in haste, belonging to different arms and services; and also the fact that people within the units did not know each other very well; and then problems with manning the units if a state of war was not declared and if men were called up for military exercises for up to 40 days and they are sent out to a theatre of war and combat operations; and also their VES is not the appropriate one, then also there is an impossibility to apply rules pertaining to a state of war in the actual situation that prevailed in the front line?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you asking the witness, Mr. Rodic, to assume all of those things and then to seek to give you an answer? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you cope with that, General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe I can. Namely, the fundamental question is how such exceptional, extraordinary circumstances influence the system of command and control. Partly, this issue was covered in my report where I drew the attention and I warned that newly formed units or the operational group or a tactical group are always in a stage of consolidation. If also the command of such a group has been formed from officers coming from different units, from different institutions and who haven't been trained as a team, that means that also the command and the entire system of command and control has to be established and develop an effective system. And as long as we don't achieve this level of efficiency, this poses a limit of the command for effective command and control.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the other system-based causes that I enumerated to you? If they exist, do they affect command and control, too?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did -- they do; namely, insufficiently consolidated units which are in the state of being formed and forming the manpower require something else, namely, more activity, more exercise of command and control than if the units had been formed in advance, trained in advance, and as such, then, subordinated to the new command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, General Zorc, in the period from the 1st of October until the 31st of December 1991, would the system of command and control encounter problems if new units were frequently brought in to the 2nd Operational Group and if existing units were withdrawn from the 2nd Operational Group? Also, because of requirements in the field, neutral resubordination of units, can all of this all together be looked upon as a problem?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could say this and confirm that the resubordination of units from one command to another, the reattachment of a unit to another command, all this requires a re-establishment of linking and communication lines among the units. And if this then goes on during battles, this is not useful for command and control as a system, and it certainly created difficulties. And if I may add, in viewing certain documents yesterday, it is my opinion that there was serious difficulties, not only on the level of the sector command to the battalion, brigade, and other subordinates, but also on the higher levels of the 9th VPS. One of the -- and this is also a part of my response to the question you have just asked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you to look at page 6 of your report. In B/C/S, it is page 6. And it has to do with the general part, the introduction, I (b) is the subparagraph, levels of command and control in the Yugoslav People's Army. Can you see the part in which you divided the system of command and control into three basic levels?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the strategic level of command and control, number 1 is the SFRY Presidency as the supreme commander of the armed force. Number 2 is the federal secretary for National Defence and the General Staff of the armed forces. And 3 - at least that is what you say in your findings - is the navy command and the air force and anti-aircraft defence command. Did such staffs exist within the strategic level of demand and control, that is?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the staff -- in my report, it says that these were commands of military districts. It is these districts which you questioned me about at the beginning of this session. Three military districts, and the military navy district, four. And the fifth, the command of the air force and anti-aircraft defence. And these were all commands on a strategic level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. In the B/C/S translation, it said something different, so that's why I wanted to clarify it. So is it correct that it is the commands of the military districts of the army. Where would you place them, the strategic level, or somewhere else actually?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I've just said. These were strategic commands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, perhaps, how the status of these commands of the military districts was regulated according to the unity plan that has to do with strategic grouping in possible theatres in the second half of the 1980s? Were commands of military districts established as forms of decentralised strategic command? Was that the situation then?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was not a term of decentralisation of command and control. It was only the third level of strategic level of command and control as I have presented it in my report. The essence of the strategic meaning of these entities, they were responsible for parts of the territory of the former Yugoslavia. And on these territories, these were battlegrounds. It was the superior to all units on that territory, the JNA units and to the units of the Territorial Defence. This does not apply to the command of the air force and anti-aircraft defence command, which covered the entire territory and the airspace over the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, into which level of command would you put the republican staffs of Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The republican staffs of Territorial Defence were and remained in this new organisation at the army operational strategic level as prior to the reorganisation were the leaderships of armies, which were on equal level as the republican staffs. In this new organisation, when the commands of military districts was set up, the republican staffs were subordinated and had an operational and strategic meaning. And they were somewhere higher than the level of the corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. General Zorc, thank you very much for your answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this concludes my cross-examination. And the Defence has a motion to make; namely, that Admiral Jokic's interview as a reference dated September 2003, which was one of the references used for the report of this witness, that the interview namely be tendered into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you have it available for tendering, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I be heard also on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we would like to use the following break to obtain that document. It's a very comprehensive interview, and the only problem we have is actually Xeroxing it. But I'm sure we can take care of that during the break and have copies delivered to the Chamber afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And you have during your cross-examination taken the general to a number of passages. From the interview of Admiral Jokic, what is it that you would want more than that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, bearing in mind the need to keep my cross-examination as brief as possible --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... We lost the English...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear the English booth now, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Rodic. I'm sorry, there was a break for a while there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Bearing in mind the need to keep my cross-examination as short as possible, the testimony and the cross-examination of the witness in relation to his very comprehensive report, and also bearing in mind the comprehensive interview given by Admiral Jokic, the Defence tried to use only a portion of the relevant material based on the interview so that we may be able to cover all other areas during our cross-examination that were relevant to our case. Therefore, we were not able to go through the whole interview as we might have liked to during our cross-examination. The interview does contain a lot more information in relation to this witness's expert report than the Defence has gone into during our cross-examination. And this information is certainly helpful for the understanding of this witness's report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, after Admiral Jokic's testimony, the same motion was raised, and this Chamber denied at the time the motion very soundly. It is not evidence. The best evidence of what Admiral Jokic says is what Admiral Jokic has said. It is clear from what this witness has indicated that there were very limited references, and the fact that the Defence chose to adopt in its questioning much more than was even contemplated for use, or in fact used, by this witness does not make it any more admissible. It is not evidence; it is not admissible as evidence. It is hundreds and hundreds of pages. And we think that the Chamber has had the benefit of its use in the cross-examination of Admiral Jokic, and perhaps it's overuse in the cross-examination of this particular witness. But it is -- Admiral Jokic appeared before this Chamber exclusively as a witness, and as such there was no basis for any admission into evidence of something that is not evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The interview with Admiral Jokic will not be received in evidence. There was some use of it made by the present witness, General Zorc. He did identify the use that he made. As far as I can judge, in most material respects, those matters were dealt with in cross-examination of the General. The interview with Admiral Jokic was explored further than that in the course of cross-examination; and in those respects, there has been some evidence from the General which may be of some use to the Defence or to the Trial Chamber. But beyond, that as Ms. Somers has submitted, the interview itself is not of direct relevance, does not constitute evidence, and ought not to be admitted. Yes, Ms. Somers, do you re-examine?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I do. Thank you, Your Honour. Re-examined by Ms. Somers:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, in the course of cross-examination, a number of questions were asked about the subordination of the 472nd Brigade during the period 1 October through 31 December 1991. Now, during that period, it is clear to you that the 9th VPS was directly subordinated to the 2nd Operational Group. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there were periods during that three-or-so month period where the 427nd Brigade was directly subordinated to the 2nd Operational Group. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were times when the brigade was directly subordinated to the command of the 2nd OG.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there were also periods when the 472nd Motorised Brigade was directly subordinated to the 9th VPS but remained within the composition of the 2nd Operational Group. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Vis brigade was - again, at certain times - resubordinated or returned under the command of the 9th VPS. However, all the units of the 2nd OG, regardless of which one of the subordinated commands commanded them, remained in the composition of the 2nd OG. And this means that the brigade, too, was in the composition of the 2nd OG.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If I may ask, please, that P100 be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask you, General, if you have in front of you, and perhaps it can be put on the ELMO if it's convenient. This is an organogram or organisational structure as of 6th December 1991. Now, according to this organisational structure, do you see the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade? Are you able to identify or locate the box that has the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is visible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this brigade [sic] which is under the direct command or directly subordinated to the 9th VPS is still within - do you agree - the structure -- sorry, the 3rd Battalion; the transcript reads "brigade"; it should read "battalion." Still within the structure, it shows still within the structure of the 2nd Operational Group. Is that correct? The 3rd Battalion of the 472nd directly subordinated shows still within the structure of the 2nd Operational Group. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. All units listed here on this chart are in the composition of the 2nd OG, only that the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd is directly subordinated to the command of the 9th VPS whereas the command of the 9th VPS is subordinated to the command of the 2nd OG. And all of these units are within the composition of the 2nd OG, including others not shown here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does that indicate, then, that on the 6th of December, which is what this particular organogram refers to, that the highest command, the highest command of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade is the command of the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can I ask you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness was about to provide an explanation. Therefore, the may the witness be allowed to explain what he was about to explain. He was interrupted in midstream, which I didn't think was fair. So please, again, the answer to the previous question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I just wanted to add that the 3rd Battalion was at the second level of subordination to the 2nd OG. So through the 9th VPS. And within the operational group, the command of the 2nd Operational Group was, of course, the highest level of command leading the operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you take a look, now, please, at the box that has the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Motorised Brigade. Do you see it? The 3rd Battalion of the 5th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see it is also under -- on the 6th of December under the direct command of the 9th VPS, and still within the structure of the 2nd Operational Group? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm, then, that on 6 December 1991 the command of the 2nd Operational Group was the highest command of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to this organisational chart, that is the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the 2nd Corps, a box for the 2nd Corps. Do you see it, General?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you see that it was -- I think that you were shown P101 earlier, a document which talks about the resubordination of the 472nd Brigade with the exception of the 3rd Battalion. Do you remember that, that it was a document showing resubordination of the 472nd except for the 3rd Battalion? That was on or about 20th of November. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. That was yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the 2nd Corps as still being directly subordinated to the 2nd Operational Group as of 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You can put that exhibit away. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, during the course of cross-examination, you were shown a document, D43, which was an order issued by General Strugar dated 25 October 1991 which, among other things, ordered the resubordination of the 472nd Motorised Brigade to the 9th VPS. Considering -- do you remember that, first? Make sure you remember.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Considering that during this period, the 9th VPS itself was directly subordinated to the 2nd Operational Group, does the fact that the 472nd Motorised Brigade -- does the fact that its being resubordinated to its so-called former parent group, does that fact diminish in any way the responsibility of the 2nd Operational Group command over the 472nd Motorised Brigade while that brigade is still within the composition of the 2nd Operational Group command?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That does not change in any way the responsibility of the command of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the order D43, which you were shown and which we have just discussed, the one of 25 October of General Strugar, does it have any impact on the overall command of General Strugar over the 472nd Motorised Brigade during the period that it is subordinated - it, meaning the brigade - is subordinated to the 9th VPS which VPS was subordinated to the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It does change the manner of command for this brigade precisely from the very moment when the brigade was resubordinated to the 9th VPS. As of this moment, the commander of the 2nd OG no longer issues direct commands to the commander of the brigade. Instead, these commands are issued by the command of the 9th VPS, and that applies to the entire new structure of the 9th VPS, including this brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the overall, highest level of command, including over the 472nd Brigade, which has just been resubordinated, is still the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And ultimate responsibility down to the last soldier for every action in that brigade or any part thereof lies with the command of the 2nd Operational Group, the commander of the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked about two orders that were issued by General Strugar. One is P121 and the other is P119.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask that the usher please provide these orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you first, General Zorc, to take a look at P119, which is dated 24 October 1991. You have been asked and you have -- sorry. Do you have it? Do you have the order in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You had been asked during the course of your cross-examination about the essential parts of a combat order, and I wonder if you would be good enough, please, to look at this order and identify the same portions that you talked about in your cross. For example, a description of the enemy. If you could just take us through this combat order and talk about its parts, please. Without reading every single detail, just identify the paragraphs that show the essential parts, please.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can do that. This order is titled "Decision for Further Action." And this is a completely normal title for such a combat order. This order contains under item 1 information concerning the manner in which the commander of the 2nd OG assesses the activities of the enemy during this time. Item 2 provides a brief assessment of the outcome achieved by his own units in the time past. Under item 3, the issuer of the order submits to his subordinates information on further combat action; and furthermore, the issuer also defines the tasks of the 37th Corps of the 2nd Corps and of the 9th VPS. In addition to that, he also defines the mission of the 472nd Motorised Brigade, meaning that it was subordinated to him at that time. Then certain missions are also defined in terms of improving combat morale, security, engineering support, supply, as well as aircraft and artillery support.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I think you've identified most of the parts. What I'd like to ask you to take a second look at is paragraph 3 where it says "I decided to..." Do you see paragraph 3, General?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, item 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this where General Strugar is issuing his orders about the mission to his subordinate units or the missions of his subordinate units? Is this the central part of the description of what is to be done?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the central part which contains a general part of the decision as well as the missions of the subordinated units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is General Strugar the only person issuing this order, this type of order, to his subordinates?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. He was the only one competent for the issuing of such a document, although the document that I have in my hand is not signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you, please, to take a look at page 1 of the order. And in paragraph 3, within the definition or the taskings, the issuing part of the order about mission, do you see where it says: "Further, to stabilise the defence at the reach lines and improve the tactical position," and then the next sentence says: "Further to, ensure the complete control of the coast movement and especially of the sea movement, focusing on the communication towards Dubrovnik from the sea, the Neretva River valley, and the Peljesac peninsula." Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is an integral part of the general tasking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this tasking indicates that there are also naval assets which are subordinated to the 2nd Operational Group, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here in this part, it only says that control has to be assured over sea traffic, maritime traffic, with a focus on access points to Dubrovnik. In addition to that, also along the River Neretva and also the Peljesac peninsula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I turn your attention to the -- in English, it's the next page.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it goes on. We're under "9th VPS." Do you see the section, General, where it addresses that -- it talks about engagement of the units. And then if goes on: "Further on, continue the control of the sea, moving an order to prevent with even more quality and" -- I believe surety, or surely -- "the ships' arrival and departure from the Dubrovnik Municipality port." Now, is this also an indication of command and control over waters in the Dubrovnik operation?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After he decided in the general part that better control has to be assured for maritime access to Dubrovnik, the mission given to the command of the 9th VPS expressly states that incoming traffic to Dubrovnik has to be protected in an even better fashion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is command and control by the commander of the 2nd Operational Group over naval forces of the 9th VPS, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what you're asking means that he does have control, but only at a second level. He gave this mission, this order, to the commander of the 9th VPS, and the commander of the 9th VPS is the one that has to carry this order out with the help of his maritime units, his naval units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. But the tasking is from the commander of the 2nd Operational Group to do this?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. That is an order issued by the commander of the 2nd Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Reading further, just below what we have discussed, it states: "I should think about the need of the strengthening of the battleships and in due course submit the request for the said to the VPO command." Now, what is being asked of the VPO command, what contribution? In other words, does that clearly reflect that the VPO is not involved in the operational activity but more in the materiel side of anything in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the essence of the mission ordered by the command of the 2nd OG to the commander of the 9th VPS is the following: If the commander of the 9th VPS will assess that he does not have sufficient naval forces to provide for more efficient control of maritime traffic incoming to Dubrovnik, then he should consider whether he would request from the command of the VPO a reinforcement of naval forces. At the same time, this is a sort of a suggestion on the part of the commander of the 2nd OG that those forces are insufficient. This was done because the commander of the 2nd OG did not have within his structure naval forces which could reinforce the command of the 9th VPS. Only the command of the VPO had at its disposal naval forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me a second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In issuing instructions concerning further action, particularly going into the next day, the command of the 2nd Operational Group -- commander -- clearly assigns tasks to the 472nd Motorised Brigade concerning combat activity which appears to go into a time frame when it was resubordinated to the 9th VPS, which was by an order you've already seen the next day. Do you agree that despite that resubordination, there is no change in the overall command authority of the 2nd Operational Group commander as to this order and as to that unit?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This unit was throughout this time in the structure of the 2nd OG regardless to which lower level of command it was resubordinated or regardless of whether it was kept under the direct command of the operational group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could take a look now at P -- I believe it was 121. It's an order dated 23rd of October 1991. And I think we've already made the correction, Your Honours, where at the top it says "2nd command," it should in English say "2nd Operational Group command" based on the Serbo-Croatian. You see a paragraph dedicated to the 9th VPS and a paragraph dedicated to the 472nd Motorised Brigade, do you not?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you confirm that the reporting of both at 0900 hours at the command post for Trebinje, is that a standard -- is that something that is expected, a normal part of an order?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is a normal request. But it does not always have to be part of an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We can move on, please. I'm sorry, General. I apologise, there was one point I wanted to ask you about on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Is it possible just for a second to put 121 back up. I just missed it in my own notes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the first paragraph, the introductory paragraph under 9th VPS on 121, that's the 23rd October order. Do you see it, General, the very first paragraph? Do you see it? Okay. Does that paragraph indicate clearly that General Strugar approves the proposal of the commander of the 9th VPS, and does that approval -- is that approval consistent with General Strugar's exclusive authority and command over the 9th VPS and all of its subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the first sentence means that the commander of the operational group accepts the proposal of the decision referred to him by the commander of the 9th VPS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by approving it, General, then General Strugar becomes responsible for the implementation of that order.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He would be responsible in any case. But through this approval, he states that he agrees with the manner of implementing the task given to the 9th VPS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. D44 was an exhibit. Defence Exhibit 44 --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm finished with that, Mr. Usher, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- that was shown to you or discussed with you during cross-examination. Would you want to see it? Would it help you to have a look at D44, please, on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have the order in front of you, General? Not yet. Sorry. Do you see the order in front of you, General Zorc?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the terms of this order, General, is it clear that by 29 September 1991 the 2nd Operational Group was tasked with the blockade of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here I have to be precise. What I have before me is the text of a decision on the part of the commander of the operational group dated 29 September which constitutes only a part of his order issued to his subordinates. This is a proposal for the decision submitted to the commander of this group to the chief of General Staff for approval. There is no item 2 here which would state what sort of task the operational group was given. Instead, we can conclude what its task would be from the general part of the decision stated under item 1, paragraph 1. And this paragraph 1 also states that the blockade of Dubrovnik from the sea and from land is one of the decisions made by the commander of the operational group. And this, then, certainly means that he received such an order from his superior commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You commented that the coming together of different groups of soldiers at various levels of preparation from various branches, various levels of training can particularly, and perhaps under circumstances such as the one that have been discussed, can be difficult. Nonetheless, does this proposal which you have seen through subsequent orders was implemented? Does it bear the expectation that these missions will be accomplished by the units in the 2nd Operational Group or under the command and control of the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. These missions are to be carried out by the units of the 2nd Operational Group regardless of what level of training they have received in general.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the context of General Strugar's authority and command over the Dubrovnik operations, including the blockade, I would like to ask you first of all if you are familiar with a publication called Narodna Armija. Are you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It is the newspaper or the magazine of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what are some of the items that are normally found in it?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this general publication which was public, just like any other newspaper, magazine, contained mainly information on events within the JNA and on events which were of particular significance for members of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would ask to have distributed, please, a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection. First of all, we object to the distribution of any kind of document, and we would seek clarification as to what this document has to do with the content of the cross-examination. What is the reason that compels my colleague to bring any kind of document into the redirect examination? We don't know what kind of document this is, and I think that it is quite inappropriate to bring in any kind of document, let alone a newspaper article that has nothing to do with the subject of our cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, you can hardly say that until you know what the document is. But perhaps we'll learn from Ms. Somers, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Shall I first seek the distribution of it, and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, you can tell us what it is. There's an objection to it being distributed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes. The article, Your Honours, is from Narodna Armija dated 22nd December 1991 and in fact discusses -- it takes a highlight of General Strugar and his various -- the various aspects of his command and authority in the 2nd Operational Group. And it is a view by the JNA on that command authority. It is very relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What aspect of the cross-examination has given rise to this issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It goes to overall authority for functions, for all command functions, in the 2nd Operational Group. There has been a suggestion that there may have been another person who had said function, and that is not what is supported by the view in the particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the view in a newspaper article is going to assist in that respect, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It is the official journal of the JNA, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we object for several reasons. The first reason is what my learned friend mentioned as a reason is precisely what the content of the report of this witness is. And I don't see how a newspaper article is going to assist her in this. Secondly, what is contained in this newspaper article are the conclusions of someone who is the author of this article. Your Honour, we do not have here before us the author of this article. We do not know on the basis of what he wrote this, on the basis of what kind of information, when we published this, why he published it. We don't know anything about this. It is highly inappropriate not knowing anything about this Z. Dervisevic who allegedly wrote this article to deal with this document any further. By the way, this is no official journal. This is simply a newspaper, a publication, which carried different articles from different spheres of life with free interpretations. And by the way, it was a public newspaper, and it was accessible to all who wanted to read it. The essence of my objection is what I said at the outset. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I raise with you further, Ms. Somers, what it is that makes it now relevant that was not present during evidence in chief? In other words, why now and not when the evidence was being led in the first place?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The challenge to the exclusive authority of General Strugar was raised in cross-examination. And the discussion in this article includes comment attributed to General Strugar about various of his subordinates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But isn't that one of the aspects to which the evidence of this witness is directed? Isn't that one of your reasons for calling this witness, to establish the exclusive authority of the accused?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. And we believe that it was sufficiently established, but it has been again challenged. And if this piece of evidence will further corroborate the views of the very military in which the accused served, it may assist the Chamber in some additional -- having some additional evidentiary value.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: There were issues of parallel command -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't realise you were in conference. The issues of parallel command were raised during cross-examination. Again, this covers some -- to the degree of reliability is always a factor that the Chamber would consider. But in terms of admissibility, it counters suggestion of any parallel chain of command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The objection of Mr. Petrovic is upheld. There appears no reason why this document could not have been advanced during evidence in chief. So first, there is no demonstrated justification for its tendering at this stage. Secondly, it is a document or a publication of no demonstrated credibility for our purposes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll move on. Is this the time at which the Chamber might wish to break? I'm not...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Zorc, despite not having seen the initial order by which the 2nd Operational Group was formed, you have seen orders, including combat orders, issued by General Strugar, as well as other orders issued in the course of the Dubrovnik operation. Do these documents which you have reviewed allow you to conclude or draw the inference that there were no limitations on General Strugar's command and control authority over the units subordinated to him in the 2nd Operational Group which included the 9th VPS and the 472nd Motorised Brigade with its various -- with all its battalions?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The documents which I saw are completely sufficient for me to make a conclusion that the commander of the 2nd Operational Group had exclusive authority for implementing the tasks conferred upon him. He had all the necessary competence to command all units subordinated to his operational group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have been asked about Article 6 of the rules of authority of the corps command of land forces in peacetime. And without going back to the specific provisions, if you remember that it has been discussed, if a unit is temporarily subordinated to another formation outside of its permanent composition for operational purposes, is it not the case that the command of the formation to which that unit was subordinated to for combat and operational purposes would have command responsibility for misconduct committed in the course of combat or for combat indiscipline committed by such subordinate unit?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. From material that you have reviewed so far, can you conclude that all of the units of the 9th VPS deployed in the area of operation of the 2nd Operational Group were within the composition of the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here, too, I have to specify my answer. Since I did not see a document that would precisely determine the limits or the outlines of the zone of responsibility of the 2nd Operational Group, particularly to the south of the entry into Boka Kotorska, because of this, I cannot make the conclusion whether the units of the 9th VPS which were located at the southernmost point of this coast were also integrated in the structure of the 2nd Operational Group. The fact is that in none of the documents that I saw did I see those units being resubordinated from the command of the 9th VPS regardless of the fact that these units - and I am here referring to the naval marine brigade - that they would come under the command of the 2nd Operational Group. I did not see any tasks conferred on such units. Also, the orders of the 9th VPS did not specify any particular missions for this brigade. And for any other units which were within the structure of the 9th VPS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Can I ask you, General, perhaps I can make my question a bit more precise. Can you conclude that the units of the 9th VPS which were involved in the area of operation of the Dubrovnik campaign of the 2nd Operational Group were within the composition of the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. All those units that in any way received orders were within the composition of the 2nd Operational Group, as is evidenced by the fact that they received those orders from the command of the 2nd OG.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked about the content of three orders of the 9th VPS in D57, D58, and D67, just for general reference. Generally, General, what is the source from which information on enemy activity and positions are gathered? Is that source through intelligence information?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Information on the enemy is called "intelligence data," and intelligence data is gathered through intelligence bodies, intelligence organs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible that sometimes intelligence information may be flawed or not provide accurate information, or could sometimes be based on mere suspicion?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To the regret of all military commanders, information on the enemy is almost never comprehensive and almost never completely reliable. And that is why we usually speak of assessments of the deployment of forces, the activities, and the intent of the enemy. That is why we do not speak of actual fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked about the improbability of a brigade commander reporting to his corps commander in relation to a special situation in the presence of a subordinate officer such as a battalion commander. Do you recall there was an example or hypothetical given to you by the Defence in cross-examination about a brigade commander reporting to his corps commander in relation to a special situation and having that situation discussed in the presence of a subordinate officer such as a battalion commander? I will turn your attention, if it will help -- if you don't, I will try to focus, and it may refresh the hypothetical given by my learned friend opposite. The evidence that has been heard in this court was that subsequent or consequent, as a consequence of the shelling of 6 December 1991 of Dubrovnik, General Strugar and Admiral Jokic were summoned by General Kadijevic to Belgrade to be present before him together about the incident. Was there anything unusual, given those circumstances, that General Strugar should be summoned on the incident in the presence of his subordinate officer, Admiral Jokic?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wouldn't say that there was anything particularly problematic with this. Granted, these are two officers that are in a relationship of subordinate and superior. However, in such a case, the manner of ascertaining responsibility has to be done by the person who decides whether this is appropriate or not. What I think would happen in such a case is the following: The federal secretary would, in fact, call on the commander of the 9th VPS in the presence of his superior. And that, then, is completely acceptable.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, I want to find a related point. I just have it on a separate question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fact that the federal secretary -- let's say you are the commander of the 2nd Operational Group. We'll use General Strugar in his role, then. The fact that the federal secretary calls General Strugar, actually calls General Strugar and not Admiral Jokic or the brigade commander of this undisciplined battalion commander who allegedly initiated an action. Does that reinforce the position that the federal secretary considers General Strugar to be in command on the 6th of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this question please be clarified. If it's a hypothesis, could its elements please be spelled out. This, what we've heard, is not clear enough. So could my learned colleague say whether it is based on evidence. And if it is not based on evidence, could she please say that it's a hypothesis. And then when presenting her hypothesis, can she then ask the general for his opinion of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Based on evidence before this Chamber, General Kadijevic contacted General Strugar. And as a result of that contact, General Strugar and Admiral Jokic went to Belgrade on the 6th of December 1991 in connection with the incident of the shelling of Dubrovnik stemming from the order -- in connection with that incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that, the fact that General Kadijevic contacted General Strugar and that along with General Strugar came Admiral Jokic, but he contacted General Strugar --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is not in evidence. Your Honour, that is not in evidence. If she wishes to quote it, then she should say where it is from. But I think, Your Honour, that this is sheer interpretation of what the evidence actually is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I am very happy to go back to the hypothetical mode, but I submit it is my belief that it is evidence. However --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It may be your belief. But you will well appreciate you can hardly expect the Chamber to have that detail at its fingertips. So if you rely on it as evidence, you need to refer us to the passage. Would you prefer to do that after the break?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I can do that. Or I can phrase the question in such a way that it will not necessarily require that, if it would be in the interests of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it the end of your examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: No, I have a few more points, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Then we'll give you the break to sort that out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to check the transcript, Your Honours. I refer to the transcript page 4063, and I will read from it, with your permission, line 8. "No, this is what I know. General Strugar called me" - this is Admiral Jokic speaking in examination-in-chief - "this is what I know. General Strugar called me and told me that General Kadijevic had called him. And he said that he was very angry, furious, because Dubrovnik was being attacked. This came as a major surprise to me. I was practically in shock. How was this possible? How did he know? Who informed him, et cetera? What did he mean Dubrovnik? I just know that at 6.00..." And then it goes on. And then moving on to page 4073, Your Honours. The response is: "General Strugar gave me the message. He told me what General Kadijevic had ordered him. Whenever I did all it took to stop the attack, I was prepared to go to Podgorica and then to join him on his way to Belgrade to the General Staff where the two of them were to report on this incident." If I may return, having hopefully --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I should indicate that on the basis of that evidence, Mr. Petrovic, I cannot intervene in the form of the question that was being put.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the way it reads here, that's fine. But the substance of what my learned colleague said before the break was as follows: General Strugar had been called by Kadijevic, and then Jokic accompanied him to Belgrade. There's a significant difference there in relation to what she has just read out to us. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I hope I've clarified that for the Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just backing up a little bit, General Zorc. In cross-examination you were asked questions about the failure or the alleged failure of Admiral Jokic and officers of the 9th VPS to stop the shelling of the Old Town on 6 December 1991. Now, the fact that the federal secretary based on what I have just indicated contacted General Strugar as the -- who was the commander of the 2nd Operational Group and did not directly contact either the corps commander, Admiral Jokic, or the brigade commander over the undisciplined battalion commander, that is, of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd, does this in your opinion reinforce the position that the federal secretary considered General Strugar to be in command on the 6th of December 1991 with respect to the incidents of shelling of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. We're not talking about hypothesis here. We are supposed to be talking about something that is allegedly in evidence. It would be good to show the witness what Admiral Jokic said at least on three different occasions; namely, that he had been called by Kadijevic, called by Adzic, and called by the commander of the military naval district. Strugar had called him, too, but no one was able to get through to him. That is in evidence. That is Admiral Jokic's entire evidence. Therefore, no one was able to get through to him and this is what happened. He was called through General Strugar. I hope we all remember that this was what Admiral Jokic said in his testimony. He justified that by saying that he had kept the relay communications open all the time, to the forward command post at Kupari. And that was allegedly why no one at the time was able to get through to him. That's what we remember, and I believe it would only be fair to show the general testifying here today that as part of Admiral Jokic's testimony and as part of the question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can certainly add the question that did the fact that Admiral Jokic's presence as commanded was assured through a communication by General Strugar help -- or reinforce the fact that General Strugar was in command over the forces shelling -- engaged in the shelling of Dubrovnik on the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Let me make it clear, Ms. Somers: You can put your question on any one of the bases supported by the evidence. But as you would appreciate, if the fact-finding is of some other basis than your question, well then the answer won't be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I think the latter formulation may best be the most helpful so it allows accounting for any other evidence. In the alternative, I can certainly put it in a hypothetical so it may be of assistance when the evidence is evaluated by the Chamber. And perhaps that might be the best thing. No, I'm sorry. I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If in fact Admiral Jokic's presence along with General Strugar was as a result of a communication to General Strugar by General Kadijevic, does that reinforce the fact that General Strugar was the commander -- was in command of the forces that day attributable -- or attributed -- whose actions were attributed to the shelling of Dubrovnik? Is the question clear enough, General?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without any doubt, the General Kadijevic considered General Strugar as the responsible subordinate [as interpreted] of the 2nd Operational Group as well as of the unit which violated the rules of engagement. And also irrespective of that, whether the commander of the operational sector and operational group were invited to Belgrade together or first one and then the second or in whatever way it was done, but the fact that he called them both to Belgrade meant that he considered them both directly responsible. In a regular situation, the best situation would be if the federal secretary only called the commander of the operational group. However, due to the importance of the event, he called both. And how he treated them during that meeting, that's a matter of his personal style.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: May I ask for a transcript, I believe, correction, page 37, line 2. What has been quoted, General, is "without any doubt, General Kadijevic considered General Strugar as a responsible," it says "subordinate" of the 2nd Operational Group. I think the term "subordinate" is in error.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your actual answer?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer was that General Kadijevic considered General Strugar as the responsible commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me just one moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I ask you now in a more hypothetical sense. If the federal secretary had called you as commander of a 2nd Operational Group to complain about the allegedly unauthorised activities of one of your battalions and has told you to inquire and stop it, what would be your reaction? Would you limit yourself to transmitting this order to your subordinate commanders, or would you engage yourself and undertake all possible efforts to carry out this order of your superior commander as soon as possible?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, if I were the commander, this commander general, as you assumed, in the first place, I would issue the necessary orders to the subordinate commander whom the unit is -- which was violating the rules. As I mentioned in my report and as I emphasised in my testimony, I said that also in this situation my responsibility would be complete in order to stop the shelling. If my order would not suffice, I would have to get involved also in other ways.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate some of the ways in which you would get involved if your order were not being complied with or implemented. Some examples.

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would depend on one's personal style of commanding of a superior officer. And for the operational implementation of my order, in the extreme situation, I would have to involve the officers of my command and send them to the unit which is violating the rules. And if we didn't succeed in that in a short period of time, then personally I would go. And in the position of that unit, I would take over the command and order a stop of shelling. All this in the function of implementing the order of the superior and of my order to stop the shelling as soon as possible. All following measures in order to determine the responsibility and assessment of responsibility of the perpetrators, that would be in a later stage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked about the commander of the 9th Naval Sector tasking a commission as a result of the 6th of December shelling to look into the allegations of damage to the Old Town of Dubrovnik. As the immediate superior commander of the 3rd Battalion in the chain of command, that is, the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade, is there anything unusual about the commander of the 9th Naval Sector taking this action?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the contrary. That would not be unusual because this battalion was directly subordinated to the commander of the 9th VPS. He would have to do all that which I have listed in my previous answer. And that would be what would be expected action of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You were asked to comment on Prosecution Exhibit P102.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If I might the usher for just a moment to show it to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, before you -- if you have the correct document, it is a document dated 5th of February 1992 from the 2nd Operational Group. It is signed -- it is an order issued by General Strugar. My sole question to you is: Is this an organisational structure of the 2nd Operational Group as it was on the 5th of February 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The document contains the organisational structure of the 2nd Operational Group. It is not an order. In fact, it is his report to the First Administration of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do all the units that are shown or depicted in this structure, are they all subordinated to General Strugar as commander of the 2nd Operational Group as of that date?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the first sentence, this is -- shows the composition is a detailed one, a detailed composition of the 2nd Operational Group as of 5th of February 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 2nd Operational Group under the command of General Strugar as of that date; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In cross-examination, you indicated that if Admiral Jokic were unhappy with any subordinate commanders belonging to the overall composition of the 2nd Operational Group such as the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade, he could submit a proposal for his removal. If such proposal for removal of a subordinate commander was not approved by General Strugar as commander of the 2nd Operational Group, could Admiral Jokic have removed that subordinate commander without General Strugar's approval?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that that would be an exceptional situation and that he would not do it without the approval of his superior commander. And if you allow me to add, even the proposal for a replacement of the commander should be coordinated with his superior commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following along that same line, if a commander of a unit belonging to the overall composition of the 2nd Operational Group such as the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 472nd Brigade, were to be promoted for his role within combat and for his role in combat activity within the 2nd Operational Group, would such proposal for promotion require General Strugar's approval? Could he be promoted for his role in combat activity within the 2nd Operational Group without General Strugar's approval?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A promotion that you were indicating, if it were an award for the successful performance of tasks, it would mean that this was an extraordinary promotion. In such a situation, it wouldn't be possible without the proposal being submitted in the regular way up to the federal secretary, along the line of chain of command, which would mean that the commander of the 2nd Operational Group would have to approve it, and also he himself would have to propose it to the federal secretary, such a promotion. But if a promotion were to take place in the regular way and he had a certain rank for a certain period of time, then this could be done by the federal secretariat itself. Of course, if the commander fulfilled all the legal conditions. In the preparations of the proposal for the promotion of the 2nd Operational Group or of the 9th VPS, they could also oppose such promotion if they assessed that such an officer did not deserve such a promotion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would a proposal by Admiral Jokic as a subordinate officer to General Strugar, would a proposal to withdraw and/or -- sorry, to withdraw a problematic brigade and/or replace its commander and chief of staff be an effective way of focusing on that problematic unit? You were asked yesterday about attention to be paid, and one of your comments indicated that a commander must also focus on problematic units. Was my question clear to you, or shall I repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kind ask you to define it more precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If there is a problematic unit, let's say, a brigade under the command of Admiral Jokic and of course ultimately under the command of General Strugar, is a way, an effective way to focus on that problematic brigade in order to deal with the problems a proposal to withdraw the brigade altogether from the area, or perhaps replace its commander and chief of staff if they were part of the problem? Is it clear to you now, General?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The measures you've mentioned as possible ones are indeed possible. They can be necessary. And they always represent the extreme means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the commander of the 9th VPS focussed his attention on a problematic unit in that way, is it also effective or sometimes necessary for the commander of the 2nd Operational Group himself to focus his attention on the problematic unit?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. This applies to all the superior officers in the chain of command. If the lower levels do not succeed in implementing certain tasks on the basis of orders and law, then the higher level commander must get involved in resolving such problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you expect the higher level commander - in this case, the commander of the 2nd Operational Group - to focus his attention on units which allegedly shelled the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the significance of the incident concerning the shelling of the Old Town, this involvement would be indeed necessary. And I would also expect of the commander of the 2nd Operational Group to get involved personally concerning this problem, particularly in view of the fact that the lower levels did not succeed in preventing or stopping this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If there were multiple incidents of alleged shelling of the Old Town of Dubrovnik - I'm not looking right now on the 6th of December, but I'm talking about the months of October and November of 1991 - would you expect the commander of the 2nd Operational Group to focus his attention on the problematic units that allegedly were involved with these alleged incidents?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly; he should get involved already with the first violation of the orders that he had issued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me. I just wanted to see if I might be able cut back on one question, which may have been answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you say one question? I thought you were debating whether there might be any further questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: There were three short ones that just came up in the last round of cross-examination, if I may ask to address those, and then stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Let's have the three quick ones, and then that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry, the remaining of this original bunch is, and then if I may, Your Honour, the three quick ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Defence showed you an artillery map which was Exhibit P160, and you commented on the location of air defence weapon. Assuming that the symbol reflects the approximate location of the weapon, what would be in your view the reaction of a commander of an operational group according to JNA doctrine knowing there was an UNESCO-protected site of high cultural heritage value located in the vicinity of this weapon? Would you foresee limitations on engaging this as a potential military objective?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood correctly this question, this refers to the map of the other side, the Defence, and I wonder whether the other officers had this map of the other side. But this isn't really fundamental. It would suffice if the intelligence organs of the 2nd Operational Group on the basis of the basic units, squads, platoons, companies, which were in the direct possibility of seeing the Old Town, if they determined that in the Old Town weapons were positioned of the opposite side, they would have to then inform about that their superiors. And all superiors from the squad, platoon, company and further-up commanders, up to the 2nd Operational Group, they could intervene through communications with the other side to remove the weapons and the units from the protected Old Town. And irrespective of data whether in the Old Town weapons had been located, weapons of the other side, the very orders issued to the units of the 2nd Operational Group confirm that the commands of the 2nd Operational Group and of the 9th VPS, they issued those orders that no shelling was to take place of the Old Town of Dubrovnik and -- irrespective whether or not units of the other side were located there. During the shelling, they were to see that the specific parts and important parts of the Old Town were not destroyed by the shelling and they were not hit by shelling and by mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On cross-examination today, you were asked about lack of military or shortage of military police, potential of shortage of military police within the 2nd Operational Group. Can the commander of the operational group order additional military police or security organs to -- can they be supplemented? Can they ask for more, if need be? Is it within their competence?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in a situation of insufficient discipline in his unit, and even in a situation where we have certain incidents concerning the shelling of targets which have been prohibited, and if he needed a greater number of military police units as he didn't have them, he would have to request it from the superior command. And that is the General Staff. He would have to propose that due to the exceptional needs that he have at his disposal a bigger military police unit for the needs that he had during the operation that was underway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred to the independence of the military police during cross-examination. Now, can a commander of the operational group order military police and/or security organs to initiate an investigation? We understand that once initiated, there is the independent. But can they order the initiation of investigative activity by the MPs or by the security organs?

utterances.speaker: MILOVAN ZORC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The organs of military police carry out their crime investigations on the basis of laws of provisions irrespective of the orders of the commanding officers to which they're subordinate.
